title: Chicago-area AccuWeather Alert for Winter Weather Advisory, several inches of snow accumulation possible in parts area Friday
text:
Chicago-area AccuWeather Alert for Winter Weather Advisory, several inches of snow accumulation possible in parts area Friday - ABC7 Chicago 
 24/7 Live Chicago & Suburban Cook Co. North Suburbs West Suburbs South Suburbs NW Indiana Snow 
 AccuWeather Alert for several inches of snow accumulation possible in parts of Chicago area Friday 
 Winter Weather Advisory in effect Friday for Cook, Will counties in Illinois and Lake County, Indiana 
 The Chicago, Illinois-area weather forecast for Friday includes a chance for the first snow of the season, especially for parts of Northwest Indiana. By Tre Ward , ABC7 Chicago Digital Team Friday, November 13, 2026 4:07AM Share CHICAGO (WLS) -- An AccuWeather Alert is in effect as parts of the Chicago area could see their first snow of the season Friday morning, with several inches of accumulation possible.
 A Winter Weather Advisory will go into effect at midnight and go until 10 a.m. Friday for parts of Cook and Will counties in Illinois and Lake County, Indiana.
 The City of Chicago will be deploying snow plows overnight, the Department of Streets and Sanitation said.
 ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch 
 The National Weather Service said wet snow will likely accumulate away from the lakeshore. ABC7 AccuWeather meteorologists said one to three inches of slushy snow are possible.
 The NWS says to plan on slippery conditions, especially on bridges and overpasses.

 Thursday morning, ABC7 AccuWeather meteorologists said there will be on-and-off again lake-effect rain in Northwest Indiana that could move over to the Illinois side Thursday afternoon.
 The rain will continue Thursday night and into Friday, with wet snowflakes possible mixed in.
 "Crews will be out overnight monitoring arterial streets, DuSable Lake Shore Drive, bridges, and overpasses to ensure roads are safe and passable for emergency vehicles, public transportation, and other travelers," the Chicago Department of Streets and Sanitation said in a statement.
